claims.text: The as-manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a homogeneous FCC matrix.
The as-manufactured alloy has minimal native or pre-existing oxidation.
Elevated-temperature degradation in this alloy is governed by synergistic selective oxidation.
Interactions among neighboring elements perturb their individual oxidation propensities in compositionally complex alloys.
Oxidizing exposure produces a multilayer scale primarily containing Cr2O3, with transient TiO2 and Al-based oxides.
A dense, continuous, coherent, and adherent oxide scale retards degradation by limiting oxygen and metal-ion transport.
Oxygen penetrates along grain boundaries and creates a shallow subsurface oxygen-enriched or internally oxidized region.
Excessive grain-boundary oxidation acts as a stress concentrator and impairs fatigue performance.
Under oxidizing conditions, a coherent and adherent scale forms and preserves the bulk FCC matrix.
Sufficiently high oxygen partial pressure promotes formation of a continuous protective scale.
Optimal oxidizing conditions produce limited grain-boundary oxidation and preserve fatigue performance and mechanical integrity.
Reducing H2/Ar atmospheres cause incomplete, discontinuous, or partially decomposed oxide scales.
Reducing conditions enhance grain-boundary oxidation relative to oxidizing conditions.
Discontinuous scales and enhanced grain-boundary oxidation under reducing or suboptimal oxidizing conditions accelerate degradation and reduce fatigue life.
The starting alloy has established mechanical strength and fatigue resistance.
The proposed mechanism is intended to apply at 700–900 K, 1 atm, and exposure durations of 10–100 hours.
Exposures outside the stated temperature, pressure, or duration boundaries may activate additional degradation mechanisms.
Oxide-scale morphology, grain-boundary oxygen content, and mechanical performance should correlate systematically with gas atmosphere if the proposed mechanism governs degradation.
